faq.a: Alhafiz is associated with the Arabic form الحافظ, whose core sense is the preserver, the protector.

faq.q: What is the origin of Alhafiz?
faq.a: Alhafiz is associated with Arabic. Al-Ḥāfiẓ ('the preserver'), a divine name; also a title for one who has memorised the Qur'an.
Yes — the underlying form الحافظ is Arabic.
Alhafiz can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Alhafiz should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. root ح ف ظ occurs in the Qur'an; الحافظ is a divine name

faq.q: What does Alhafiz mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Alhafiz is rendered حافظ and carries the sense حافظ، محافظ.

faq.q: What does Alhafiz mean in Persian?
faq.a: No verified Persian form was established for Alhafiz.
A romanized syllable approximation is al-ha-fiz. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Alhafiz?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Alhafiz, alhafiz. Script forms are الحافظ, حافظ, हाफ़िज़.

faq.q: Is Alhafiz a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
